judgements.justification: B's meta-review restated the abstract, named no weakness, and said the authors 'illustrated how to further boost adversarial robustness' against aQh1's 'The robustness improvement is limited'; A's meta-review carried 7cFv's two reservations forward.
The wrong claims (aQh1's CIFAR-10-only limitation, cKPT's Figure 5(a) reading) were minor and did not set either committee's score or tier.

A's concession that pre-training is needed did not leave A higher than its information supported: A's area chair kept the reservations and gave the lower tier, and B's response held no damaging admission.
No objection or score cut came after the response period; the only late action, cKPT's 2021-09-01 edit, was a raise.
B's area chair did not cite the scores alone but its own reading ('a hot research topic', 'will interest many readers'), so the split is not a pure threshold difference.
A's area chair followed its most specific reviewer, 7cFv, and B's area chair followed its own reading, not the mean of less-informed reviewers.
B's scores stayed flat because no B reviewer replied, not because B's concerns were beyond what a response could fix; the authors answered them with new results.
Stage 1 finds no outlier in either committee; all ratings sit within one point of the mean.
No reviewer's score stood apart from its committee, so no outlying score stood unrevised.
Neither area chair set aside an outlying low score or framed the meta-review as accept or reject against a detractor.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit as a ground against the paper.
B's meta-review paraphrased the paper and made no statement about the reviewers' final positions or the rebuttal; its omission of weaknesses is R14, not a misstatement of the record.
No B reviewer replied to the 2021-08-10 responses (ClusTR comparison, wrong-hierarchy ablation, TRADES), so B's pre-rebuttal 6/7/6 stood, while all three A reviewers engaged and revised.
No reviewer said they could not verify the results; confidences are 5/4/3 on both sides.
Neither committee split evenly between accept and reject; all final ratings are 5 or above.
The TRADES figures differ (52.80/53.71 to B, 52.98/53.68 over five seeds to A) only because A asked for seed averages; the accounts agree in substance.
All six reviewers praised the novelty, and no novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work; aQh1's ClusTR question was answered.
B's meta-review did state grounds for the spotlight, topical interest and expected readership; the weakness of those grounds is R01 and R02.
No reviewer contested the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
No reviewer on either side rated well above accept (top rating 7 in both), and each committee's 7 came from a light review.
Neither committee rejected the paper or judged promised revisions too large for camera-ready.
Neither meta-review relies on an assessment absent from the committee's record.
Both committees judged the paper as an analysis-plus-method paper on the same terms; neither imposed a contribution-type standard the other did not.
No score stayed below threshold, and 7cFv's held concerns (linearization link, seed variance) are central, not peripheral.
